extracted.intended_audience: lawmakers, legislative staff, civic organizations, local officials, residents, reporters, and advocates
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of POPVOX's civic-technology products that structure and connect legislative and local public information to support discovery, provenance, participation, and institutional memory. Describes product goals and feature-level desiderata for public-facing and institution-facing civic intelligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connected legislative data for discovery, trust, and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Connects bills, members, committees, hearings, witnesses, organizations, documents, and legislative histories into a public experience designed for discovery, trust, and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create relationships among diverse legislative entities so users can discover relevant items and understand them in context; the page lists specific entities to be linked (bills, members, committees, hearings, witnesses, organizations, documents, legislative histories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent public record of public input
rubrics_metrics.description: A platform for people to weigh in on legislation and create a transparent public record for lawmakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports public participation that is visible to lawmakers and the public, with the stated goal of making participation more meaningful, more accountable, and more useful to the policymaking process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic technology with institutional memory
rubrics_metrics.description: Civic technology that preserves institutional memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain historical records and legislative histories so past inputs, decisions, and documents remain accessible over time (the phrase 'institutional memory' signals retention and retrievability of prior data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured, searchable local public records (LocAlmanac)
rubrics_metrics.description: Turns local public information into structured, searchable records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize and normalize local sources so they become queryable; LocAlmanac is city-scoped and intended to convert local feeds into structured records for residents and officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingest varied public sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Ingests articles, calendars, meetings, event feeds, and other public sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support multiple input types and feeds to build a comprehensive record of local public information; implies robust ingestion pipelines and source normalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve provenance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep source attribution and traceability for records so users can verify origins; tied to the platform goal of trust and citation-backed usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support citation-backed search and Q&A
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports citation-backed search and Q&A so residents, reporters, advocates, and local officials can understand what is happening in their community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable search and question-answering features that return results with citations/backing, facilitating trustworthy discovery and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools for lawmakers, staff, and institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Builds public-facing civic intelligence products, including POPVOX.com and tools for lawmakers, staff, organizations, and institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Products should serve both public users and institutional workflows (lawmakers/staff), implying features for institutional consumption and decision support as well as public transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernize lawmaking with AI-era capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuilt for now — 'Legislative intelligence for the AI era.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied expectation to use modern techniques (including AI) to connect, analyze, and present legislative information for improved discovery, context, and trust; the page positions product redevelopment around contemporary technological capabilities.
